abstract_snippet: We present EG-CFG (Execution-Guided Classifier-Free Guidance), a novel approach to neural code generation that incorporates real-time execution signals into the LLM generation process. The method employs beam search to sample candidate completions per line, executes them against test cases, and uses execution traces as guidance signals via CFG. Achieves SotA on MBPP (96.6%), HumanEval (99.4%), HumanEval-ET (89.0%), DS-1000 (69.9%), and CodeContests (60.6%).
what_the_paper_supports: EG-CFG introduces real-time execution-guided code generation: (1) beam search samples candidate line completions, (2) AST-based extraction ensures syntactic validity, (3) candidates executed against test cases producing structured execution traces (event type, line number, variable values/types, return values, exceptions), (4) execution traces injected as dynamic signal via Classifier-Free Guidance, (5) parallel multi-agent exploration with different hyperparameters. Key results: SotA on 5 benchmarks using open-source DeepSeek-V3, outperforming methods using GPT-4. Execution traces are comprehensive: each event εk = (Ek, ℓk, vk, τk, rk, xk) captures event type, line, variables, types, return value, exceptions.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: No formal specification language (GAP-015). No formal equivalence checking (GAP-017 — only test case pass/fail). No versioning of generated programs (GAP-019). No formal verification of correctness (GAP-020 — empirical test case validation only). No persistent registry of synthesized programs. Method requires test cases at inference time — cannot generate code without them. CFG guidance strength γ is manually tuned. Parallel agents are independent — no inter-agent communication or learning.
paper_core_claims: EG-CFG dynamically incorporates execution signals into LLM code generation via Classifier-Free Guidance
Beam search samples candidate line completions; AST extraction ensures syntactic validity; execution against test cases produces structured traces
Execution traces include event type, line number, variable values/types, return values, and exceptions
Parallel multi-agent inference: multiple agents with different hyperparameters explore diverse paths
SotA on MBPP (96.6%), HumanEval (99.4%), HumanEval-ET (89.0%), DS-1000 (69.9%), CodeContests (60.6%) using open-source DeepSeek-V3
Outperforms methods using GPT-4 and GPT-4o on multiple benchmarks

GAP-015.reason: Test cases + problem description as implicit specification. No formal spec language.

GAP-016.reason: EG-CFG compiles execution feedback into guidance signal: candidates → execution → traces → CFG conditioning. This is a dynamic compilation from execution behavior to generation guidance.

GAP-017.reason: Only test case pass/fail as equivalence. No formal equivalence checking between different candidate solutions.

GAP-018.reason: Execution traces are detailed: each event captures variable state, types, return values, exceptions. This is a concrete, structured state/effect model at the line level.

GAP-019.reason: Test cases serve as validation regime, but no versioning or registry of generated programs or traces.

GAP-020.reason: No formal verification. Correctness only checked via test cases. Execution traces provide debugging information but not proof of correctness.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Problem description + test cases as implicit spec. No formal function specification language.

N2_Representation.reason: Structured execution traces as representation: (Ek, ℓk, vk, τk, rk, xk) per event. AST-based code representation. CFG conditioning as dual representation (unconditional + execution-guided).

N3_Compiler.reason: EG-CFG pipeline: candidates → AST extraction → execution → traces → CFG signal. This is a feedback compilation loop, but not a traditional spec→artifact compiler.

N4_Artifact.reason: Generated programs are artifacts, but ephemeral. No persistent storage, no metadata, no registry.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Python runtime as interpreter. Custom debugger produces structured execution traces. AST parsing as syntactic interpretation gate.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Comprehensive execution traces: each event εk = (event_type, line_number, variable_values, variable_types, return_value, exception_details). This is the most detailed execution trace model in the batch so far. Traces are per-line, per-test-case, per-candidate.

N7_Validator.reason: Test cases as executable validation. AST parsing as syntactic validation. Execution traces as diagnostic validation. Multi-tier: syntactic (AST) + semantic (execution) + functional (test cases).

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Parallel multi-agent exploration with different hyperparameters. Each agent independently explores different reasoning paths. But no inter-agent composition or routing — agents are independent and first-to-finish wins.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: No versioning, registry, or retrieval of generated programs or execution traces.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Requires test cases at inference time — cannot generate code without them
CFG guidance strength γ is manually tuned (0, 0.5, 1, 3)
Parallel agents are independent — no inter-agent learning or communication
Execution feedback is only pass/fail + trace — no semantic analysis of failures
AST extraction may modify candidates (appending 'pass', removing lines) — could change semantics
Beam search with s=3 candidates per line is computationally expensive (multiple LLM calls per line)
Only tested with Python — unclear generalization to other languages
SotA results depend on DeepSeek-V3 — unclear if gains transfer to other LLMs
No formal verification — test case pass does not guarantee correctness
strengths_noted: N6 ExecutionTrace: most detailed trace model in the review batch — per-event structured tuples
Multi-tier validation: AST (syntactic) + execution (semantic) + test cases (functional)
SotA on 5 benchmarks using open-source model, outperforming GPT-4-based methods
Parallel multi-agent exploration is practical and scalable
CFG as guidance mechanism is novel for code generation
Comprehensive evaluation across diverse task types (basic, competitive, data science)
